children: Year-ahead business inflation expectations increased to +2.4% in September vs. +2.2% in August, according to a survey released by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta on Wednesday.
Year-ahead unit cost expectations have fallen considerably since hitting a peak of +3.8% in April 2022, but remain somewhat elevated relative to their pre-pandemic average of +2.0%.
Long-run (five to 10 years ahead) unit cost expectations remained constant at +2.8%.
On outlook for employment and their realized and expected wage costs, most firms anticipate either little to no change in staffing or plan to increase levels over the next year.

When looking at the growth rates in employment across sectors, manufacturing and corporate services anticipate the strongest growth going forward. Wages have steadily increased over the past 12 month and are expected to continue to increase over the next 12 months. However, this growth rate when compared to the present inflation rate isn't nearly as strong, the survey said.

title: Business inflation expectations drift higher in September: Atlanta Fed
